channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Focal Muscle Vibration for Upper Limb Spasticity After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found that focal muscle vibration (FMV) can improve upper limb spasticity after stroke, with effects potentially moderated by frequency, amplitude, or target joint.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Sensorimotor effects of heatwrap and exercise in acute low back pain: results of a randomised controlled trial
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (N=99) found that heatwrap combined with exercise was more effective than sham heatwrap in improving pain sensitivity, lumbar muscle activity, current pain intensity, and trunk flexion range of motion in acute low back pain.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Tailoring Resistance Exercise for Knee Osteoarthritis: An Intervention Systematic Review With Dose-Response Meta-analysis of the Effects of Intensity and Volume.
item.description: A systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of RCTs found dose-response relationships between isotonic lower extremity resistance exercise volume and outcomes of pain, function, and strength in people with knee osteoarthritis (OA), and compared different intensities and delivery methods.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Efficacy of Exercise Therapy for Nonspecific Chronic Low Back Pain According to the FITT Principle: A Systematic Review With Meta-analyses.
item.description: A systematic review with meta-analyses evaluated the efficacy of exercise therapy interventions, differing in frequency, intensity, type, and time (FITT), on disability in individuals with nonspecific chronic low back pain (LBP).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Biofeedback in Parkinson's disease: A systematic review with meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review with meta-analysis found that biofeedback added to practice significantly improves lower limb activity in individuals with Parkinson's disease compared to practice alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Carrying an unseen weight: the neuro-perceptual landscape of limb heaviness after stroke- a scoping review.
item.description: A scoping review identified perceived limb heaviness as an under-recognized stroke symptom, often unrelated to weakness or spasticity. Proposed mechanisms include altered sensorimotor integration, impaired proprioception, and disrupted body representation, suggesting issues in sensorimotor processing.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: White Matter Diffusion Anisotropy and the Effects of Inpatient Multidisciplinary Rehabilitation in Parkinson's Disease: A Diffusion Tensor Imaging Analysis.
item.description: A diffusion tensor imaging analysis found that pretreatment corticospinal tract fractional anisotropy predicted responsiveness to an 8-week inpatient multidisciplinary rehabilitation program in 94 Parkinson's disease patients, with responders showing significant UPDRS Part III improvement.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of Aquatic Tai Chi and Computer Assisted Rehabilitation Environment-Based Virtual Reality Training on Rehabilitation in Patients with Parkinson Disease: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A single-blind RCT with 50 Parkinson's disease patients (Hoehn-Yahr stage 2-3) compared 12 weeks of aquatic Tai Chi (n=26) versus Computer Assisted Rehabilitation Environment-based virtual reality training (n=24). Both interventions led to improvements in UPDRS-III, BBS, TUG, and 6-minute walk test.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physiotherapist-led care for musculoskeletal conditions in the emergency department (RESHAP-ED): a randomised controlled trial with economic evaluation.
item.description: The RESHAP-ED pragmatic RCT evaluated physiotherapist-led care for musculoskeletal conditions in five Australian emergency departments, demonstrating improved effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness compared to usual care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of high-intensity laser therapy and extracorporeal shock wave therapy for the treatment of plantar flexor spasticity in post-stroke patients.
item.description: This prospective, randomized, controlled, parallel-group clinical trial with 42 stroke patients compared high-intensity laser therapy and extracorporeal shock wave therapy, each combined with rehabilitation, versus rehabilitation alone, for treating plantar flexor spasticity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Application of non-invasive electroencephalogram-based brain-computer interfaces in post-stroke hand function rehabilitation.
item.description: This article reviews the application of non-invasive EEG-based brain-computer interfaces (BCI) for post-stroke hand function rehabilitation. BCI decodes imagined hand movements to drive exoskeletons, FES, or VR devices, aiming to remodel neural pathways and promote motor recovery.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Home-based digital exercise versus hospital physiotherapy for plantar fasciitis: a propensity-score-matched retrospective cohort study with dual-perspective cost-utility evaluation.
item.description: A propensity-score-matched retrospective cohort study in China found that a 12-week home-based digital exercise program was non-inferior to hospital-supervised physiotherapy for plantar fasciitis regarding first-step morning pain (adjusted mean difference -0.63 points, 95% CI -0.92 to -0.35; p < 0.001) and showed cost-utility advantages from both payer and societal perspectives.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The effectiveness of instrument-assisted soft tissue mobilization on pain and function in patients with musculoskeletal disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 RCTs (n=550) found that instrument-assisted soft tissue mobilization (IASTM) significantly improved pain (SMD -0.74; 95% CI -1.04 to -0.44) and function (SMD -0.66; 95% CI -0.99 to -0.34) in musculoskeletal disorders in the short term, with moderate effect sizes.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Effects of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation and Individualized Physical Therapy on Pain and Function in Individuals With Chronic Knee Pain: A Pilot Study.
item.description: A preliminary triple-blinded, randomized, and sham-controlled pilot study found that 5 sessions of active tDCS followed by individualized PT improved pain and function in individuals with chronic knee pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Ideal Versus Actual School-Based Physiotherapy Practice in Israel: A National Survey.
item.description: A national survey of 202 and 152 physiotherapists in Israel compared actual versus ideal school-based physiotherapy practice across 30 items related to evaluation, IEP development, service delivery, team functioning, and administrative support.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Patient-reported knee osteoarthritis problems and rehabilitation goals: A qualitative study.
item.description: A qualitative study analyzing data from 387 participants with chronic knee osteoarthritis pain identified activity limitations and pain as the worst aspects of their condition, with rehabilitation goals centered on improving these functional issues.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical therapists as first-contact providers for musculoskeletal disorders: comparing beliefs across chiropractors, nurse practitioners, Physical therapists, and physician assistants.
item.description: This cross-sectional survey compared the beliefs of chiropractors, nurse practitioners, physical therapists, and physician assistants regarding their capabilities, educational preparation, and scope of practice in providing first-contact care for musculoskeletal disorders.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The use of eHealth in primary physiotherapy care: a mixed-method study.
item.description: A mixed-methods study in Denmark explored eHealth use among 121 primary care physiotherapists, finding basic digital tools like email and phone were common, while more advanced technologies were rarely used due to perceived barriers.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Functional Electrical Stimulation and Stroke Rehabilitation Research: The Critical Role of Sham Control Groups.
item.description: A commentary discusses the critical role of sham control groups in functional electrical stimulation (FES) and stroke rehabilitation research, emphasizing the importance of rigorous study design.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Living with stroke-related visual impairment: a qualitative exploration of lived experience, self-management, and support needs.
item.description: A qualitative study explored the lived experiences of 16 community-dwelling adults in Scotland with stroke-related visual impairment (SRVI), identifying daily impact, self-management strategies, and unmet support needs.
item.author: PubMed
